source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    To check BMC dedicate port speed status is normal.
1. Power on system
2. Connect RJ45 cable to port
3. Adjust speed under OS

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. System should be no error
2. Internet should work normally
3. Check LED by speed

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Speed status: read the RJ45/port speed + link state sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ip -s link 2>&1 | grep -A3 -E 'eth|eno'; ethtool eth0 2>&1 | grep -iE 'Speed|Link detected|Duplex' 2>&1".
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the NIC speed/link/duplex so the user confirms the port is at the expected negotiated speed.

original_test_intent: Validate speed-dependent behaviour of the port identified by the source as the dedicated BMC RJ45 connection, including error-free operation, network connectivity and the corresponding physical LED indication.
original_method: Power the system, connect the specified cable, change a speed setting under the OS, verify connectivity and errors, and visually compare the RJ45 LED with the expected speed indication.
manual_activity: Cable insertion and the LED-by-speed observation require an engineer. More importantly, an owner must first resolve whether the target is a host-managed NIC or a BMC-dedicated interface before any OS setting is changed.
required_inputs: Owner clarification of the intended physical port and control plane
Board/BMC/NIC mapping by connector, MAC and PCI identity where applicable
Approved speed/duplex/autoneg cases and peer/cable capabilities
Defined meaning of 'Internet should work normally' and its endpoint
LED mapping, maintenance authorization and restoration plan
safety_requirements: Do not run the provided command against eth0 by name; interface naming and function are not established.
Do not change speed on the only management path without an independent console/OOB recovery route.
Do not place credentials in sshpass command arguments or disable host-key verification for formal execution.
Stop on target ambiguity, link loss, duplicate address or inability to restore the original setting; do not retry automatically.
agent_execution_scope: After owner resolution, collect read-only stable interface identity, link modes, counters and before/after configuration.
Apply only an approved reversible speed matrix on the confirmed controllable interface and test the defined endpoint.
Correlate operator-supplied LED evidence and report tool results separately from the engineer verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve the source contradiction and identify the actual controllable interface/port.
Approve peer, speed matrix, connectivity criterion and rollback path.
Connect the cable, observe the speed LED and issue PASS/FAIL after evidence review.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not suitable as written. It hard-codes eth0, only reads state, duplicates an sshpass fragment in the historical CSV form, exposes password use and does not implement speed adjustment, connectivity acceptance or LED observation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Only after target resolution, map by stable MAC/PCI identity, capture full `ethtool <iface>` state and use a project-approved reversible setting command. Keep credentials out of process arguments and preserve complete output.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Power-on, cable connection, OS speed adjustment, no-error/connectivity/LED criteria, script reference and 1/0-minute fields are retained; no missing speed value is invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Split the resolved plan into stable interface mapping, approved speed transition, endpoint traffic check, counter/error review, human LED correlation and exact restoration. Use the repository script only after inspecting its target-selection and rollback behaviour.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Undetermined until the owner states whether this is a BMC controller interface, a shared NC-SI path or a host NIC.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record OS, driver/firmware, ethtool and switch/BMC versions after resolution.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform NIC/BMC architecture, board schematic and project network/LED specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the control plane and recovery explicit while retaining every original acceptance dimension.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No speed or LED case is removed; automation cannot begin until the target ambiguity is resolved.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Owner semantic decision and project speed matrix.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An OS command aimed at the wrong NIC can sever host or management connectivity without testing the named dedicated BMC port.

project_override_considerations: A project may identify a host NIC or supported BMC interface and approve a finite speed matrix, peer, endpoint and LED mapping. That override resolves this case for the project but does not rewrite the master wording. A reduced matrix must be reported as the approved project plan, not as completion of unspecified broader coverage.
expected_evidence: Owner decision identifying target port and control plane
Stable connector/MAC/PCI/BMC mapping plus peer/cable and speed/LED matrix
Before/after settings, negotiation, error counters and defined endpoint results for each approved speed
Timestamped operator LED evidence, restored final configuration and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source names a dedicated BMC port but instructs the operator to adjust its speed under the host OS and then verify 'Internet'. Without an architecture/mapping that exposes this exact port to the OS, these statements identify different control planes and cannot safely select a target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Execution is blocked because the necessary operation target is semantically unresolved; changing a guessed OS interface could disrupt service while failing to exercise the named dedicated BMC port. Missing speed/endpoint values alone would be readiness inputs, but the target contradiction requires owner resolution.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Reject YES and the eth0 assumption; its read-only query does not cover the source operation or visual criterion.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain its prerequisites and safety controls, but escalate from PARTIAL because it did not resolve the dedicated-BMC-versus-host-OS target contradiction.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Records a narrow SOURCE_CONFLICT instead of inventing a mapping, while preserving a conditional post-resolution automation plan.

review_improvement: Prevents a high-impact configuration change on an arbitrary host interface and distinguishes true target ambiguity from ordinary missing project parameters.
independent_technical_reasoning: Speed negotiation, counters and endpoint traffic can be automated on a confirmed controllable NIC, while the LED remains manual. Here the source does not establish that the dedicated BMC connector is that NIC, so classification cannot safely be PARTIAL until the owner resolves the control-plane contradiction.
